hints: Focus on what makes a carbon chiral, it must be joined to four completely different groups.
Draw out the hexan-3-ol chain with its four methyl branches, C3 has the OH group and C4 and C5 each have one methyl.
Check C3, C4 and C5 one by one for repeated groups, especially where two methyl groups appear on the same carbon.
walkthrough:
**Draw the carbon skeleton**

Let's build the molecule together. Start with hexan-3-ol, a 6-carbon chain with OH on C3, then add methyls at 2,2 and at 4 and 5.

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$$

**Recall the chiral test**

A chiral carbon has four single bonds to four different atoms or groups. If any two groups are the same, it is not chiral.

**Test C3**

C3 is joined to H, to OH, to a $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$ group on the left (C2 side), and to a $\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$ group on the right (C4 side). All four are different, so C3 is chiral.

**Test C4 and C5**

C4 is joined to H, to $\text{CH}_3$, to $\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$ on the left, and to $\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$ on the right. All four are different, so C4 is chiral. C5 is joined to H, to $\text{CH}_3$ (branch), to $\text{CH}_3$ (C6), and to the C4 chain. Because it has two identical methyl groups, C5 is not chiral.

**Count them up**

C2 has three methyl groups so it cannot be chiral. Only C3 and C4 qualify, giving 2 chiral carbon atoms in total.

options.A: Only 1 is too few. Many students spot C3 with the OH as chiral but miss C4, which also has four different groups (H, methyl, left side and right side).
options.B: Correct. C3 and C4 each carry four different groups and are chiral, while C2 has three methyls and C5 has two methyls so neither is chiral. Total is 2.
options.C: 3 is one too many. This comes from wrongly counting C5 as chiral and forgetting that C5 is bonded to two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups (its branch methyl and C6).
options.D: 4 is far too many. This comes from assuming every branched carbon is chiral, but C2 has repeated methyl groups and C5 has repeated methyl groups, so neither can be chiral.
